_comment: Expected values for the structured-extraction eval.
Each case names a fixture, the domain that selects the schema, and the
fields that are scored. A field is CORRECT only when every fragment in
must_contain is present AND no fragment in must_not_contain is.
must_not_contain is the distractor list, and it is what stops the metric
saturating. Every entry is a near miss that exists in the same document:
last year's revenue, the signature date rather than the effective date,
the arbitration seat rather than the governing law, a cited paper's
authors, a family-history condition, a discontinued drug. An answer that
hedges by listing candidates fails, because listing candidates is not
Fields NOT listed here are unscored. Some schema fields have no answer in
a given fixture (a quarterly report has no `guidance` beyond the outlook
line, a discharge summary has no `patient_id` worth asserting beyond the
MRN) and asserting on them would measure the fixture, not the extractor.

revenue.note: 388.1 is prior year, 401.2 is Q2, 430-445 is guidance, 96.4 and 214.5 are segments

net_income.note: 61.2 is operating income, 180.3 is gross profit

eps.note: 2.14 is diluted. 2.21 (basic) is NOT treated as a distractor: the schema says only 'Earnings per share' and does not name a basis, so an answer giving both, labelled, is correct. Requiring its absence scored a preference the system was never told.

fiscal_period.note: Either spelling is correct. The model answered 'Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 2025' and the first version of this case called it wrong for not saying 'Q3', which scored format. 'q2' was also listed as a distractor and removed: the document never writes 'Q2', only 'second quarter', so that assertion could never fire. Caught by test_every_distractor_appears_in_its_document.

guidance.note: guidance is the forward range, not the reported quarter

risks.note: all three named risks; a partial list is incomplete, not wrong

parties.note: Barrowfield is the guarantor; the other two are law firms

effective_date.note: 14 Feb is the signature date, 3 Jun is an amendment

governing_law.note: New York is the arbitration seat, not the governing law

penalties.note: 0.5 percent per week capped at 8 percent; the 2 percent service credit is explicitly not a penalty

authors.note: the four excluded names are authors of CITED work

hypothesis.note: a third-order correction over 0-60 C removes most thermal drift

datasets.note: the two excluded corpora are named only as related work

diagnoses.note: PE was ruled out; coronary artery disease and asthma are family history

procedures.note: CT pulmonary angiogram also acceptable but bronchoscopy is unambiguous

physician.note: Ngoma is the referring physician, explicitly not responsible for inpatient care

patient_id.note: INVERTED on purpose. The schema field reads 'Patient identifier or MRN (anonymise if present)', so emitting the raw MRN is the FAILURE and withholding it is correct. The first version of this case demanded the MRN, which asserted a violation of the schema's own instruction and scored the model wrong for obeying it. Now it tests that the anonymisation instruction is actually honoured.

organisations.note: The schema asks for 'Named organisations or companies', which Brandt and Fielding is. Excluding it asserted a semantic the schema does not state. See RESULTS.md: the General schema's fields are enumerative and cannot be scored for exclusion.

locations.note: Same: 'Named locations, cities, countries'. Porto and Rotterdam are both named locations in the document, whatever their relationship to the company.

monetary_values.note: Same: 'Monetary amounts with currency'. All three figures are monetary amounts stated in the document.
